title: instrumentation: add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, and microbench harness for kernels & batching
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production latency regressions were difficult to attribute to kernels, scheduling, or KV cache interactions without lightweight instrumentation. This PR adds NVTX ranges (CPU/GPU hop-aware), a set of atomic counters for hot-path events, and a small microbenchmark harness to exercise kernels, KV cache, and continuous batching outside e2e stack. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: lightweight NVTX emitter and macros (C++) to mark kernel launch, forward/backward-like passes, KV cache lookup/hit/miss, batching enqueue/dequeue. 2) counters: atomic counters exposed via the existing metrics registry; added labels for model, shard, and batch_size. 3) microbench: new bench target (bench/kernel_bench) with scripts to run kernels with synthetic inputs and measure median/p99 latencies; includes a GPU warmup and optional NVTX recording. 4) dashboards: added a perf dashboard JSON with NVTX-annotated waterfall visualizations and counters time-series for latency breakdown. 5) CI: new perf job that runs microbench on a dedicated perf runner; CI gating is advisory (does not block merges) but reports regressions. Checklist: - [x] NVTX macros and header added - [x] Counters wired into runtime hot paths (scheduling, KV cache, batching) - [x] Microbench harness + small python wrapper for offline runs - [x] Docs: instrumentation guide & how to record NVTX traces - [x] Dashboard panels and Grafana import JSON - [x] Unit tests for metrics plumbing Non-goals: not enabling tracing by default in prod; this is opt-in via env var REDWOOD_INSTRUMENTATION=1. Compatibility/rollout: feature gated via runtime flag; metrics are no-op when instrumentation disabled. How to use: enable REDWOOD_INSTRUMENTATION and run the bench scripts under tools/microbench; upload the NVTX .nvp file to the perf dashboard importer described in docs. Impact: adds ~80 bytes of static metadata per NVTX range and minimal atomic increments on the hot path; measured overhead in local microbench <1% median latency on our test models. Follow-ups: wire counters to sampled traces sent to the perf pipeline (ENG-1501), add auto-alerts for p99 regressions (ENG-1423).
